title: Model catalog demo - Everspring Health
summary: AE + SE walkthrough of Redwood's model catalog focused on open models selection, benchmarking methodology, and compatibility with Everspring's on-prem GPU fleet. Customer concerned about latency vs cost, quantization compatibility, and SOC2/network constraints. Agreed next steps: send sizing and pricing, share SOC2 and network diagram, schedule a 2-week performance POC with sample prompts.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-19
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Lee (AE), Marco Ruiz (SE) - Redwood; Dr. Aisha Khan (CTO), Liam O'Connor (Head of MLOps), Priya Patel (Security Lead) - Everspring Health

Summary (auto-generated): Quick model catalog demo highlighting open model options, benchmark numbers, and a compatibility matrix for on-prem GPUs. Discussion of hosted vs dedicated, cost/latency tradeoffs, and security requirements.

[00:00] Jasmine: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jasmine from Redwood, and with me is Marco, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Aisha: Hi Jasmine, thanks. Good. We just finished a standup so perfect timing.
[00:17] Marco: Great, I can do a quick screen share of the model catalog and some benchmark slides. Sound good?
[00:23] Liam: Yep, keen to see the open model options — we prefer open models if possible for licensing.
[00:29] Priya: And I'll be listening for encryption and SOC2 compliance details.
[00:34] Jasmine: Perfect. Quick intro — the goal today is to show how you can pick open models from Redwood's catalog, look at verified benchmarks, and review compatibility with your on-prem A100/H100 nodes. Then we can talk about next steps for a POC.
[00:48] Marco: Jumping in — here's the model catalog. We surface community open models and our curated variants. Each entry includes latency p95 on our hosted runs, token cost, and notes about quantization and KV cache support.
[01:05] Marco: You'll see models categorized by capability — small, medium, LLM-large, and instruction-tuned. We also tag models that are recommended for batching or for low-latency single-shot calls.
[01:20] Liam: Quick question, how does Redwood verify latency numbers? Our ops team wants reproducibility.
[01:26] Marco: Good question. We run standardized runs across different sequence lengths and batch sizes, using a fixed prompt set per workload class. The numbers in the catalog are medians from multiple runs; we also publish the raw run sheets upon request. There can be noise — sometimes the transcribe pipeline shows different names like 'Redwood Dedicate' — that's just a small thing in older logs.
[01:50] Aisha: Are the benchmark runs on the exact hardware profiles? We run both A100 80GB and an H100 cluster.
[01:57] Marco: We have profiles for both. In the compatibility matrix we map model variants to driver/CUDA/CuDNN versions and recommended quantization settings. For A100 we typically recommend 4-bit quantization for large models to save memory, H100 can sometimes run int8 pathways depending on the build.
[02:18] Priya: When you say quantization recommendations, do you mean Redwood provides pre-quantized checkpoints or a toolchain to quantize?
[02:25] Marco: We provide both: vendor-verified quantized artifacts for popular models, plus our compile-time quantization tool that aligns with your runtime kernels. There are caveats — some model ops may not fuse well with certain quant configs and that shows up with minor quality regression which we flag.
[02:44] Liam: If we pick an open model, say llama2-13b-type variant or Mistral-like opensource, do you manage the checkpoint or do we bring our own?
[02:52] Jasmine: You can either use the hosted artifact from Redwood's catalog — we host verified weights and manage versions — or bring your own checkpoint into Redwood Private. Many enterprise customers prefer to bring their own for compliance.
[03:08] Aisha: For compliance, the Private deployment is attractive. Does the audit trail include per-request logs? We need full auditability for claims.
[03:16] Marco: Yes, Private includes audit logs, request/response tracing hooks, and integration with your SIEM. We can redact sensitive fields at ingestion and you can configure retention. It ties in with KMS for envelope encryption.
[03:29] Priya: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys and HSM integrations?
[03:33] Marco: Yes, we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM via KMIP in Private deployments. Hosted can use Redwood-managed keys if that's acceptable.
[03:42] Liam: Back to benchmarks — what's the typical latency delta between hosted and dedicated for us? We're trying to decide if the cost of Dedicated is justified for our low-latency SLA (p95 < 120ms for 512 tokens).
[03:55] Marco: It depends on workload. For single-token generation with small batch sizes, Dedicated with pinned GPUs typically reduces p95 by 20-35% compared to multi-tenant hosted instances, because you avoid cold-starts and get more predictable kernel selection. For heavy batching, hosted bursts can sometimes be more cost-efficient. We'll show some sample numbers.
[04:14] Marco: (shares slide) Here's a p95 table: model X on H100 hosted 0.18s, dedicated 0.12s at 1-2 concurrent requests. Cost per token shifts accordingly — our Optimize tool models unit economics.
[04:30] Liam: Can we run a pilot on our infra to validate? We want to see real numbers with our prompts.
[04:35] Jasmine: Absolutely. Typical approach is a 2-week POC: we deploy Redwood Private on a small subset of your cluster or run Redwood Dedicated with a mirrored config, run your prompt set, and capture latency/cost/accuracy.
[04:47] Aisha: What about operator overhead? We are small infra-wise. We prefer as-managed as possible.
[04:53] Jasmine: For ops-lite customers we recommend Redwood Dedicated — we handle the runtime and maintenance, you get predictable throughput. For full control, Redwood Private is installable and we provide automation scripts and a support tier.
[05:05] Priya: One more on security: does Dedicated offer VPC peering and private networking? We cannot expose PHI over public internet.
[05:12] Marco: Yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering, private endpoints, and private link options. For Private (on-prem), obviously it runs inside your network. We can also do encrypted transit and strict egress rules.
[05:24] Liam: Compatibility matrix — can you walk us through an example for H100 with CUDA 12.2?
[05:31] Marco: Sure. In the comp matrix we list tested driver versions, container images, recommended kernel builds, and any flags like TF32 off/on. For CUDA 12.2 on H100 we recommend kernel build r3, quantization profile Q4_0 or Q4_1 depending on model. I'll attach the exact matrix after the call.
[05:50] Aisha: Do you have any open models you particularly recommend for our clinical summarization workload? We need high factual accuracy.
[05:58] Marco: For accuracy we often start with instruction-tuned variants of Llama2-13B or Mistral large-family models. We also include evals for summarization F1/ROUGE scores in the catalog. For higher accuracy, some teams prefer a 16B instruction-tuned checkpoint if latency budgets allow.
[06:15] Liam: How does Redwood handle rolling model updates? If we pin a model, can we test a canary before switching?
[06:22] Jasmine: Yes — Console supports rollouts: canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback. You can pin versions and schedule rollbacks.
[06:30] Priya: Any compliance packs for healthcare — HIPAA support?
[06:34] Jasmine: We have HIPAA customers on Dedicated and Private. We provide BAAs through our legal and support teams; we also have options for on-prem-only data flow. We'll connect you with legal after this call.
[06:45] Liam: A few nitty-gritty items — driver versions and cuDNN mismatches have bitten us before. Do you provide a docker/container image we can run on our nodes?
[06:54] Marco: Yes, we publish container images pinned to tested combos. In Private you run our runtime image; we provide an installer and a compatibility checker script that validates drivers, nvidia-smi, and kernel.
[07:07] Aisha: About model selection — can we filter catalog by token-cost/p95/quality?
[07:12] Marco: Yep. In the Console you can filter by cost per 1k tokens, latency p95, model size, and tags like "quant-friendly", "low-latency", "instruction-tuned". Also we link to benchmark run sheets for reproducibility.
[07:26] Liam: On the topic of quantization, do you see quality regressions for our clinical text when using 4-bit?
[07:34] Marco: It depends on model architecture and prompt. We run A/B evals on a held-out clinical prompt set — sometimes 4-bit introduces minor regressions on tricky reasoning tasks. We flag those models and provide fallback variants. That's part of what Optimize does: it recommends quantization profiles per workload and runs a quality delta check.
[07:54] Priya: If we do Dedicated, what's the SLA and how are incidents handled?
[07:59] Jasmine: Dedicated includes an uptime SLA and priority support. Incidents are routed to a dedicated support channel, and we provide runbooks and playbooks for on-call.
[08:09] Aisha: Cost question — can you ballpark cost for a 4-GPU Dedicated pool vs hosted for our expected QPS?
[08:17] Marco: Roughly, a 4x H100 Dedicated pool amortized monthly will be higher baseline than pay-as-you-go hosted, but per-token unit cost often drops if you reach steady utilization. We can run a cost model given your QPS and token lengths — that's part of the pricing worksheet we'll send.
[08:33] Liam: For the POC, we want to run 3 models: small instruction-tuned (for short summaries), 13B family, and a 16B family for high-fidelity. Can Redwood host all three and route requests per policy?
[08:45] Marco: Yes, the routing layer supports per-route model assignments, fallback policies, and automatic degradation paths to lower-cost variants if latency spikes.
[08:56] Jasmine: Let's talk POC logistics briefly — we need your sample prompt set, target KPIs, and access method (we can run against hosted with masked PHI or deploy Private into your cluster). Liam, which do you prefer?
[09:09] Liam: Prefer running on our infra if possible, but we can start hosted masked for a fast baseline while Private setup is in progress.
[09:17] Aisha: Timeline — we're aiming to decide by end of September for Q4 rollout. Does that align with Redwood's onboarding time?
[09:24] Jasmine: Yes, that'll work. A 2-week POC in late August/early September gives time for procurement in mid-September.
[09:31] Priya: Procurement — any standard contract terms or unique clauses for data residency?
[09:36] Jasmine: We have templates and can add clauses for residency and retention. Our legal team will work with you. We'll include a SOC2 report and a sample DPA.
[09:45] Marco: (screen shows compatibility matrix) Example: model Y — tested on CUDA 12.1/12.2, driver 535+, works with q4_0 but q8 paths are experimental on H100. Notes: disable TF32 for stable numerics on certain builds.
[10:04] Liam: That level of detail is helpful. Please attach the matrix and the exact container tags.
[10:09] Marco: Will do.
[10:12] Aisha: Recap for us: POC, pricing, compatibility matrix, SOC2 and legal templates.
[10:20] Jasmine: Correct. We'll send the sizing worksheet and propose POC dates. Marco will attach the comp matrix and quant notes.
[10:27] Priya: One last thing — are there any known gotchas with mixed GPU fleets? We have a mix of A100s and a few older V100s.
[10:36] Marco: Mixed fleets work but you should avoid mixing model variants on nodes with very different compute characteristics for the same route. We can recommend placement policies. For older V100s certain newer kernels aren't supported — we'll flag those in the matrix.
[10:52] Liam: Great. If you can get the pricing worksheet by Friday, procurement can start initial review.
[10:58] Jasmine: We'll send it by Friday EOD.
[11:02] Aisha: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the POC.
[11:05] Marco: Thanks, we'll follow up with the attachments and next steps.
[11:09] End of meeting
